tweets: Calling external contracts can transfer control flow before your function finishes, allowing another contract to execute first.
In a reentrancy attack, a malicious contract calls back into the original contract while the first invocation is still active.
This allows multiple invocations of the same function to interact in ways that may not be intended by the developer.
To prevent this, perform all internal state changes before making any external calls.
This approach is known as the Checks-Effects-Interactions pattern.
Alternatively, you can use a reentrancy lock mechanism like OpenZeppelin's ReentrancyGuard.
